standard.title: Plan, create, edit and publish written and multimodal texts
standard.description: plan, create, edit and publish written and multimodal texts, organising, expanding and developing ideas through experimenting with text structures, language features, literary devices and multimodal features for specific purposes and audiences in ways that may be imaginative, reflective, informative, persuasive, analytical and/or critical
standard.prior_knowledge: Students plan, create and publish texts developing ideas critically, selecting features for complex purposes and audiences (AC9E9LY06). They have not yet planned, created, edited and published written and multimodal texts that experiment with text structures, language features, literary devices and multimodal features across the full range of text purposes.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students plan, create, edit and publish written and multimodal texts, organising, expanding and developing ideas through experimenting with text structures, language features, literary devices and multimodal features for specific purposes and audiences.

nodes.label: Planning for purpose and audience
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can plan a written or multimodal text by identifying purpose, audience and key ideas, and selecting appropriate text structures and features for those choices.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce a plan for a text that identifies purpose, audience, key ideas and at least two structural or feature choices with a rationale for each.
nodes.typical_width: Develop a detailed plan for a written or multimodal text that organises and expands ideas, selects text structures and features appropriate to the purpose and audience, and previews the argument or structure.
wider: Plan a persuasive text that previews the argument structure explicitly — outlining major points, evidence and conclusion — before drafting
Plan a multimodal text that integrates navigation, text, sound and moving/still images, considering how each mode serves the audience
Plan a text that addresses a First Nations Australian community audience, considering how purpose, audience and cultural context shape structural and feature choices
success_criteria: Identifies the purpose and audience of the planned text
Selects at least two structural or language feature choices with a rationale connected to purpose and audience

nodes.label: Creating texts with developed ideas
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create written and multimodal texts that develop and expand ideas through deliberate use of text structures, language features, literary devices and multimodal features.
nodes.minimum_width: Create a text that develops ideas through at least two deliberate feature choices (structural, language or multimodal), with evidence of experimentation.
nodes.typical_width: Create a written or multimodal text that organises, expands and develops ideas through deliberate experimentation with text structures, language features, literary devices and/or multimodal features for a specific purpose and audience.
wider: Create a written text that compels readers to empathise with ideas and emotions expressed or implied, using deliberate literary and structural choices
Design a webpage that combines navigation, text, sound, and moving and still images for a specific audience, making deliberate structural choices about how the modes work together
Create a multimodal text that addresses a complex real-world issue for a specific audience, experimenting with how different modes contribute to an analytical or critical purpose
nodes.hinge_reason: Node 3 (editing and publishing) requires students to have a created text to review, revise and reflect on — without a substantive creation, editing is reduced to surface error-correction rather than purposeful revision.

response_modes.reason: Students who only create in one mode or for one purpose develop a narrow repertoire — experimentation across written and multimodal contexts builds transferable understanding of how features serve different purposes.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Webpage and multimodal design tasks offer rich creative depth — the choices required to coordinate navigation, text, sound and image for a specific audience are substantially more complex than single-mode writing.
success_criteria: Creates a text that develops ideas through deliberate feature choices
Demonstrates experimentation with at least one text structure, language feature or multimodal element

nodes.label: Editing and publishing with reflection
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can review, edit and refine texts for accuracy and purpose, and reflect on choices made and how they might develop further.
nodes.minimum_width: Edit a text making at least two specific revisions to grammar, spelling, vocabulary or structure, and reflect on at least one choice made.
nodes.typical_width: Review and edit a written or multimodal text for accuracy of grammar, spelling and punctuation and to achieve specific purposes and address particular audiences, reflecting on how choices may be changed or developed in future texts.
wider: Conduct a structured self-editing process using an editing checklist that covers grammar, vocabulary precision, structural effectiveness and audience impact
Share a draft with a peer and use their response to guide a revision round, reflecting on how reader feedback informed editing decisions
Publish a final text to a real audience (school publication, competition) and reflect on how the publishing context shaped final editing decisions

response_modes.reason: Editing integrates the planning and creation phases — students must coordinate their original intentions with what the text actually achieves; this phase collapse risk is real if students treat editing as merely correcting errors rather than purposeful revision.

success_criteria: Makes at least two specific editing revisions with a stated reason
Reflects on at least one choice made in the text and how it might be developed further
